speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound shows a cystic mass in the subhepatic region with bile duct dilation, which is highly suggestive of a tumor in the head of the pancreas or ampulla of Vater. To confirm the diagnosis and assess resectability, I need to visualize the mass and surrounding structures more clearly. REQUEST TEST: CT Scan of Abdomen

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT scan contradicts the ultrasound findings of a mass, suggesting the "cystic mass" may actually be a dilated common bile duct rather than a tumor. Given the painless jaundice and dilated ducts without a visible mass, this presentation is classic for benign strictures or stones, so I need to visualize the biliary tree directly to identify the obstruction. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRCP and CT scans suggest the obstruction is not due to a mass or large stone, pointing towards a microscopic pathology like cholangiocarcinoma or a small ampullary lesion missed by imaging. I need to directly visualize the bile ducts and pancreas to find the source of the obstruction. REQUEST TEST: ERCP

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal imaging studies despite clear signs of biliary obstruction are highly unusual and suggest a functional or microscopic cause rather than a structural blockage. I need to know if you have any history of autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis or inflammatory bowel disease, to evaluate for primary sclerosing cholangitis or other autoimmune liver conditions.

text: Given the classic presentation of painless jaundice, weight loss, and a dilated common bile duct without a visible mass on CT, MRCP, or ERCP, this is highly suggestive of an ampullary carcinoma that was missed by imaging. DIAGNOSIS READY: Ampullary Carcinoma
